chapter: Chano Pozo, Town Hall and Charlie Parker
title: Parker's frustration and the Carnegie Hall replacement story
summary: After "No Noise", Granz was always looking for replacements; Machito explains Parker's frustration at being tolerated rather than accepted.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: The first recording you made with Parker is "No Noise", Part I and II. Is that right?
Okay, as a result of that record were there any personal appearance with Charlie Parker after that?

At the Carnegie Hall, so is a very interesting story about it. Ahh, Norman Granz was like a scout like. He was all over the place looking for somebody to replace somebody, because Norman Granz is a very independent person. If he say I am going to give you one-thousand dollars, he would give you one-thousand dollars, no matter how. The man of his word. On account that he is that way, he don't like to be pushed around by so-called a star, so he always looking for somebody that could replace you.

In that particular time, ah Dizzy, I mean Charlie Parker was in his uproar, let's say. You know, he has his emotional problems - in account that he was so far-advanced - that he wasn't openly accepted as much as other musicians that wasn't, play half of the way he was producing, so that for frustration create a problem. That happen to any human being. He don't want to be tolerated, he want to be accepted; but he was producing, so you know, tolerance and acceptance look like love and infatuation. You know, people make a big mistake from infatuation and real love; - so he knew the difference between accepted and tolerance.- and to be playing for people that they don't know what he was playing, because even the people
that were associated with them had problems to understand what Charlie Parker was playing. The same happened with Dizzy Gillespie.
